title: Clefts & fronting
note: it-clefts (agreement of be, that vs who, fronted adverbial keeps its preposition, not until / because of) · wh-clefts incl. What + do + be + bare infinitive and singular be before a plural focus · the reason (why) … is that … (never is because) and All (that) … is … · fronting without inversion, contrasted with the inversion unit · emphatic do/does/did · 4 strands x 12 · 48 items · built to live 2026-08-07 (cloud run 12)

cards.title: Clefts: one sentence, split in two
cards.title_cz: Klefty: jedna věta rozdělená na dvě
cards.body: A cleft takes a sentence you could say in one clause and splits it into two, so that one element sits in the spotlight and the rest is presented as already known. No new facts are added — only the packaging changes. Czech does this with word order and with stress; English word order is too fixed for that, so it builds a frame instead.
cards.body_cz: Kleft vezme větu, kterou byste řekli jedním celkem, a rozdělí ji na dvě části tak, aby jeden prvek stál ve světle reflektoru a zbytek se tvářil jako už známý. Nepřidává žádnou novou informaci — mění se jen zabalení. Čeština to dělá slovosledem a přízvukem; anglický slovosled je na to příliš pevný, a tak si staví celou vazbu.

table.caption: one plain sentence, four packagings
rows: plain
Her advice saved the project.
it-cleft
It was her advice that saved the project.
wh-cleft
What saved the project was her advice.
all-cleft
All that saved the project was her advice.

cards.title: The it-cleft
cards.body: it + be + the focus + that. Use who instead of that when the focus is a person. The be belongs to it, so it is always is or was — it never becomes are, however plural the focus is.
cards.body_cz: it + be + zdůrazněný prvek + that. Je-li zdůrazněným prvkem osoba, místo that se dá who. Sloveso be patří k it, takže je vždy is nebo was — nikdy se nemění na are, ať je zdůrazněný prvek jakkoli v množném čísle.

table.caption: what can go in the spotlight
rows: person
It was Petr who broke the window.
thing
It is the deadline that worries me.
place
It was in Brno that we first met.
reason
It was because of the rain that we cancelled the trip.
time
It was not until midnight that the results appeared.

points: A fronted adverbial keeps its preposition: It was in Brno that…, not It was Brno that…
It will be the students who lose most. — the tense of be follows the sentence, the number never does.
Negate the focus, not the frame: It is not the money that matters to them.

cards.title: The wh-cleft
cards.body: Also called a pseudo-cleft. The known part goes into a what-clause at the front and the focus lands after be. The what-clause counts as one singular thing, so be stays singular even before a plural focus.
cards.body_cz: Také se mu říká pseudo-cleft. Známá část jde do vedlejší věty s what na začátek a zdůrazněný prvek přijde až za sloveso be. Věta s what se počítá jako jedna věc v jednotném čísle, takže be zůstává v jednotném čísle i před množným zdůrazněným prvkem.

table.caption: what goes after be
rows: noun phrase
What I need is a quiet room.
plural noun phrase
What we need is more chairs.
action
What he did was call the police.
to-infinitive
What they decided was to postpone the meeting.
whole clause
What the report shows is that costs have gone up sharply.

points: After What + subject + do + be, the verb is a bare infinitive: What he did was call…, not was called.
What we need is more chairs. — is, not are. This is the mistake to watch for.
What, never that or which: ✗ That she wants is more time.

cards.title: The reason … and All …
cards.title_cz: Vazby s the reason a s all
cards.body: Two more frames with the same job. The reason (why) … is that … names a cause. All (that) … is … means 'the only thing' — the that is usually dropped, and the frame is a common polite way of making a request sound small.
cards.body_cz: Další dvě vazby se stejnou funkcí. The reason (why) … is that … pojmenuje příčinu. All (that) … is … znamená „jediné, co…“ — that se obvykle vypouští a celá vazba je běžný zdvořilý způsob, jak zmenšit váhu vlastní žádosti.

table.caption: the second half
rows: the reason why … was + noun
The reason why she left was the noise.
the reason … is that + clause
The reason I called is that I need your advice.
the reason for + noun
The reason for the delay was bad weather.
All … is + noun
All I want is an honest answer.
All … do is + bare infinitive
All you have to do is sign here.

points: ✗ The reason is because… — after the reason … is, English wants that.
All she needs is a few days off. — singular is again, exactly as in the wh-cleft.
All we did was wait. — bare infinitive after was, the same rule as What he did was call…

cards.title: Fronting and emphatic do
cards.body: Fronting moves an object or an adverbial to the front to contrast it with something else or to pick up what the previous sentence ended on. The crucial point is that the subject and the verb do NOT swap — that is what separates fronting from inversion. Emphatic do insists that the verb is true.
cards.body_cz: Fronting posune předmět nebo příslovečné určení dopředu, aby ho postavil do kontrastu s něčím jiným nebo navázal na konec předchozí věty. Klíčové je, že podmět a sloveso si NEvymění místa — právě tím se fronting liší od inverze. Emfatické do trvá na tom, že sloveso platí.

table.caption: fronting vs inversion
rows: This book
I finished in two days.
That part of the report
I have already read.
Such details
we can talk about later.
Never again (negative → inversion)
will I make that mistake.

points: Only a negative or limiting element forces inversion. A plain fronted object does not.
His first novel I have never managed to finish. — never sits inside, so no inversion.
do / does / did + bare infinitive: She does know the answer, not She does knows.
In speech the stress falls on do; in writing the word itself carries the emphasis.

cards.title: Common mistakes

table.caption: check
rows: It were the students who lost most.

What we need are more chairs.

What he did was called the police.
What he did was call the police.
The reason I called is because I need your advice.
The reason I called is that I need your advice.
All what I want is an honest answer.
All I want is an honest answer.
This book finished I in two days.
This book I finished in two days.
She does knows the answer.
She does know the answer.

points: Czech can put the focus last and lean on it with the voice; English has to build one of these frames instead.

Chceme-li zdůraznit děj, použijeme What + podmět + do + be + infinitiv bez to: What he did was call the police.

items.explanation: Fronting moves an object or an adverbial to the front for contrast or to link back to what came before. Unlike inversion, the subject and the verb keep their normal order. Emphatic do puts do / does / did in front of a bare infinitive to insist that the verb is true; the main verb then loses its own ending.
items.explanation_cz: Fronting posune předmět nebo příslovečné určení na začátek věty kvůli kontrastu nebo kvůli návaznosti na předchozí větu. Na rozdíl od inverze si podmět se slovesem ponechají normální pořadí. Emfatické do postaví do / does / did před infinitiv bez to a tvrdí tím, že sloveso platí; hlavní sloveso pak ztrácí vlastní koncovku.
